title: Guidelines for use of Satellite Phones in Bhutan (2019)
text:
Guidelines for Satellite Phones

1. Introduction
A satellite phone (‘sat phone’) is a mobile phone that helps you communicate by connecting to
orbiting satellites instead of terrestrial cell phone towers. These phones are quite commonly
used during disaster and emergencies for search and rescue operations particularly in
geographically ‘difficult’ places where normal cell phones are not able to operate. Even though
satellite phones can be useful for travelers and during times of emergencies yet in certain
countries the use of satellite phones is either restricted or completely banned probably due to the
threat of terrorism.
In consideration of the benefits as well as a host of issues associated with satellite phones, the
Bhutan InfoComm and Media Authority issues these guidelines for use of satellite phones in
Bhutan. The use of satellite phones in Bhutan shall be governed by these guidelines issued as per
the provisions of section 58 of Information, Communication and Media (ICM) Act of Bhutan,
2018.
2. Objective
These guidelines are issued to provide clarity to organizations and individuals particularly
visitors on the laws that govern the import and use of satellite phones in Bhutan.
3. Conditions for import and use of satellite phones
3.1 The import of satellite phones into the country shall be permitted only with prior permission
from the Authority.
3.2 Import and use of satellite phones shall be allowed only to the following:
a) Government agencies associated with national security, disaster management and
medical emergencies.
b) Embassies and international organizations officially stationed in the country.
c) Aviation sector requiring emergency communication facility.
d) During the official visit of state-guest.
e) Local tour companies for its clients.
3.3 For the purpose of subsection 3.2 (d) and (e) above, the use of satellite phone is time bound
and shall be re-exported.

3.4 The Authority shall determine the type of satellite phone that may be used within the
Country based on national priorities, government policies and industry trends.
3.5 The Authority shall cancel the permit or confiscate the satellite phone whichever is
applicable in the event of an inappropriate or illegal usage. The applicant shall be denied the
opportunity of using satellite phone in future in case of violation.
4. Procedure for obtaining permit from the Authority
4.1 The application for import and use of satellite phones must be applied to the Authority as per
the application form in Annexure 1 of the guidelines. The application shall be accompanied
by an undertaking letter as prescribed in Annexure 2 of the guideline.
4.2 The application form shall be accompanied with an administrative fee of Nu. 2500.00 per
phone. However, the Authority shall exempt this fee for subsection 3.2 (a) and (d) above.
5. Obligation of satellite phone permit holder
After obtaining the permit from the Authority, the permit holder shall:
a) Not share or hire out the satellite phone to any other organization or individual.
b) Not change the type of satellite phone without prior approval of the Authority.
c) Inform the Authority if the permit holder plans to terminate the use of the satellite
phone.
d) Submit any information sought by the Authority.
e) Cooperate with the Authority on any matters related to satellite phones and in the
enforcement of these guidelines.
